# Architecture: layers, boundaries, and where things go

This document exists to answer one question without a debate: **where does this
code go?** And to make a second question answerable by a machine rather than a
reviewer: **is this import allowed?**

The failure mode it prevents is specific. An agent or a hurried developer
needing somewhere to put a function creates a file, then a directory, then a
`utils/` folder, and six weeks later nobody can find anything and every change
touches five places. Structure is not decoration; it is what keeps the cost of
the tenth change the same as the cost of the first.

**Every rule here is enforced in CI.** An unenforced convention is a
suggestion, and suggestions lose to deadlines.

---

## 1. The dependency rule

One rule, and everything else follows from it:

> **Dependencies point inward and downward. Never sideways, never upward.**

Inner layers know nothing about outer layers. A pure function does not know a
database exists. A repository does not know an HTTP route exists. A design-system
button does not know a feature exists.

Concretely, for the frontend, outermost to innermost:

```
app/            routes. The only layer expo-router knows about
  |
features/       vertical slices. Where product code lives
  |
components/ui/  design-system primitives
data/           query cache + api client
stores/         client state
services/       adapters to the outside world
  |
contracts/      entities, api shapes, constants  (shared with backend)
lib/            pure functions. No I/O, no React, no imports from above
```

And for the backend:

```
routes/         HTTP edge. Validate, authorize, delegate. No logic
  |
services/       business logic
  |
repositories/   data access. SQL lives here and nowhere else
effects/        outbound side effects: storage, queue, email
  |
contracts/      entities, api shapes, constants  (shared with frontend)
lib/            pure functions
```

---

## 2. What each layer is, and what it may import

### Shared, `packages/contracts/`

The contract between app and backend. **Imported by both. Imports nothing.**

| Directory | Holds | Never holds |
|---|---|---|
| `entities/` | Domain types and value objects. `Submission`, `Wall`, `Prompt`, `AccountClass`. Pure shapes plus pure invariants | I/O, framework types, database column names |
| `api/` | Request and response shape per endpoint, one file per resource | Logic, defaults that differ by caller |
| `constants/` | Enums and fixed values that both sides must agree on: the six inks, brush sizes, channel kinds, story character cap | Anything that changes per environment. That is config or a flag |
| `flags.ts` | The typed feature-flag registry | Flag values. Only declarations |

If a type is used on one side only, it does not belong here. This package is the
agreement, not a dumping ground for types.

### Frontend

| Layer | Purpose | May import | Must never import |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app/` | expo-router routes. **Thin.** A route file wires a screen and nothing else. Ideally under 50 lines | `features/*` public index, `components/ui`, `theme` | `services`, `data`, `repositories`, another route |
| `features/<name>/` | A vertical slice of product. Owns its own components, hooks, actions, selectors | Its own subtree, `components/ui`, `data`, `stores`, `services`, `contracts`, `lib`, `hooks` | **Another feature's internals.** Cross-feature access goes through the public `index.ts`, and needing it often means the boundary is wrong |
| `features/<name>/actions/` | User intent. Orchestrates services and stores. "Submit the drawing", "accept the invite" | `services`, `stores`, `data`, `contracts`, `lib` | React components, navigation internals |
| `features/<name>/hooks/` | React binding for this feature | Its own actions and selectors, `data`, `stores` | Another feature |
| `features/<name>/selectors/` | Derive view data from store or cache state. **Pure** | `contracts`, `lib` | Anything with I/O |
| `components/ui/` | Design-system primitives. Button, Text, Card, Icon | `theme`, `lib` | `services`, `stores`, `data`, `features`. **A primitive that knows about a feature is not a primitive** |
| `data/` | Query cache config and the typed API client. One place that knows how to talk to our backend | `contracts`, `services/http`, `lib` | `stores`, `features`, React components |
| `stores/` | Client state only: draft, session hydration, UI. Zustand | `contracts`, `lib` | `services`, `data`. **Stores hold no server data** and perform no I/O. Actions orchestrate; stores remember |
| `services/` | Adapters to the outside world: auth, media, notifications, telemetry, crash, flags. Interface plus adapters plus factory | `contracts`, `lib` | React, `stores`, `features`. A service is callable from a test with no renderer |
| `theme/` | The themes map and semantic tokens | `lib` | Everything else |
| `hooks/` | Cross-feature hooks only. If one feature uses it, it belongs to that feature | `data`, `stores`, `contracts`, `lib` | `features` |
| `lib/` | **Pure functions. No I/O, no React, no clock, no randomness passed implicitly.** Date arithmetic, formatting, stroke geometry | `contracts` | Everything else. If it needs an import from above, it is not pure and does not belong here |
| `providers/` | The provider tree, one file per provider | `services`, `data`, `stores`, `theme` | `features` |
| `linking/` | The one deep-link and notification payload resolver | `contracts`, `lib` | `services`, `features` |

### Backend

| Layer | Purpose | May import | Must never import |
|---|---|---|---|
| `routes/` | HTTP edge. Validate input against a schema, authorize, delegate to a service, map the result. **No business logic, no SQL** | `authz`, `services`, `contracts` | `repositories` directly, another route |
| `authz/` | **The single authorization choke point.** Membership, ownership, block relationships, account class | `repositories`, `contracts`, `lib` | `services`, `routes`, **the feature-flag client** |
| `services/` | Business logic. Orchestrates repositories and effects inside a transaction boundary | `repositories`, `effects`, `authz`, `contracts`, `lib` | `routes`, HTTP types, `req`/`res` |
| `repositories/` | Data access. **All SQL lives here and only here**, parameterized | `db`, `contracts`, `lib` | `services`, `routes`, `effects` |
| `effects/` | Outbound side effects: S3, queue publish, email, push dispatch. Injected, so tests substitute | `contracts`, `lib` | `services`, `repositories` |
| `db/` | Pool, transactions, migration runner | `lib` | Everything else |
| `lib/` | Pure functions | `contracts` | Everything else |

---

## 3. Where does this go? The decision table

Consult in order. Stop at the first match.

| If it... | It goes in |
|---|---|
| is a type both app and backend must agree on | `packages/contracts/entities` or `/api` |
| is a fixed value both sides must agree on | `packages/contracts/constants` |
| is a pure function with no I/O | `lib/`, in a file named for what it does |
| talks to the network, disk, keychain or a vendor SDK | `services/<thing>/`, behind an interface with two adapters |
| is a React component used by one feature | that feature's `components/` |
| is a React component with no product knowledge, reused | `components/ui/` |
| is user intent that coordinates several things | that feature's `actions/` |
| derives display data from state, purely | that feature's `selectors/` |
| remembers something the user is doing right now | `stores/` |
| caches something the server owns | `data/`, via the query cache. **Not a store** |
| is SQL | `backend/src/repositories/`. Nowhere else |
| decides whether someone is allowed to do something | `backend/src/authz/`. Nowhere else |
| is business logic | `backend/src/services/` |
| sends something outward | `backend/src/effects/` |
| is none of the above | **Stop. Ask.** Add a line to `code-questions.md`. It is more likely the boundary is wrong than that a new layer is needed |

---

## 3b. The platform boundary: what Android inherits

iOS ships first and Android is a fast follow with no Android engineer in this
phase. That makes the boundary a decision to take **now, while the codebase is
small**, rather than a discovery in month three. Drawing it after three sprints
of iOS-shaped code is what turns the fast follow into a rewrite.

The rule is simple and it is the layering above, read a second way:

> **Everything except the platform edge is written once. The platform edge is
> the only place a second implementation is allowed.**

| Layer | Android inherits | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/contracts` | Unchanged | It is the API agreement. There is nothing platform-specific in a type |
| `lib/` | Unchanged | Pure functions. If a pure function needs a platform check, it is not pure and it is in the wrong layer |
| `services/` interfaces | Unchanged | The interface is the contract. Only the adapter behind it varies |
| `data/`, `stores/`, `selectors/`, `actions/` | Unchanged | No rendering, no platform API. This is where most of the product logic lives, and it is the point of the split |
| `features/*` hooks and components | Almost entirely | React Native renders both. Divergence here should be a layout decision, not a logic one |
| `components/ui/` | Mostly, with per-platform styling | Type scale, shadow and touch feedback differ by platform convention. The component API does not |
| `services/*` **adapters** | **Replaced** | Secure storage, biometrics, push registration, audio, file access. This is the platform edge |
| Native modules and config | **Replaced** | Entitlements, permission declarations, signing, build config |

**Three rules that keep it true:**

- **`Platform.OS` checks live in `services/` adapters and in styling, nowhere
  else.** A `Platform.OS` branch inside a feature's action or selector is
  platform logic that has leaked into shared code, and it is the exact thing that
  makes the second platform expensive. Treat one in a pull request as a design
  question, not a detail.
- **Use the `.ios.ts` / `.android.ts` file convention rather than inline
  branching** when an adapter genuinely differs. The boundary is then visible in
  the file tree rather than buried in a conditional, and the shared file has no
  platform awareness at all.
- **No iOS-only concept in a shared type.** If a contract or entity names
  something that only exists on one platform, the abstraction is at the wrong
  level.

**This section is the artifact the client-architecture spike asks for**, and it
should be promoted to an ADR alongside the compute one. It is recorded here
rather than only in an ADR because it is a rule the boundary checker can partly
enforce, and a rule nobody can check decays.

## 4. Anti-sprawl rules

These are the rules that keep the codebase navigable at month six. They are the
direct answer to "I do not want agents adding file after file."

**Extend before you add.** Before creating a file, look for the module that
already owns this concern. When you do add one, be able to say what you
considered extending and why it did not fit. If you cannot, extend it.

**Banned directory names**, everywhere, no exceptions: `utils`, `helpers`,
`common`, `shared`, `misc`, `core`, `base`, `stuff`. Every one becomes a
landfill, because a name that means anything means nothing. Pure functions go in
`lib/` in a file named for its subject (`lib/prompt-day.ts`, not
`lib/utils.ts`). A "helper" for one feature belongs to that feature.

**No new top-level directory without an ADR.** Adding a layer is an
architectural change. It gets one page saying what it is for and what may import
it, or it does not happen.

**One public surface per feature.** `features/<name>/index.ts` exports what the
rest of the app may use. Everything else is internal. A deep import into another
feature's subtree is a CI failure.

**No barrel files except a feature's `index.ts`.** An `index.ts` that re-exports
a whole directory destroys tree-shaking, creates import cycles, and makes
"who uses this?" unanswerable.

**One primary export per file.** One React component per file, named the same as
the file. Small pure helpers may share a file when they share a subject.

**Soft caps, as signals not laws.** A file past ~300 lines or a function past
~50 usually means two responsibilities in one place. Not a build failure. A
prompt to look.

**Delete as readily as you add.** Dead code is worse than missing code because it
still has to be read and maintained. If a flag has been on for a month, remove
the flag and the dead branch.

**Colocate tests.** `submit-drawing.ts` and `submit-drawing.test.ts` side by
side. A distant `__tests__` tree is how tests get orphaned when code moves.

---

## 5. Naming

Consistency matters more than the specific choice, so these are settled and not
worth relitigating.

| Thing | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Directories | kebab-case | `features/daily-prompt/` |
| React components | PascalCase, file matches export | `PromptCard.tsx` |
| Everything else | kebab-case | `submit-drawing.ts`, `prompt-day.ts` |
| Hooks | `use` prefix | `useTodayPrompt.ts` |
| Actions | verb first, what it does | `submit-drawing.ts`, `accept-invite.ts` |
| Types and interfaces | PascalCase, no `I` prefix | `Submission`, not `ISubmission` |
| Constants | SCREAMING_SNAKE for true constants | `STORY_CHAR_LIMIT` |
| Booleans | `is`, `has`, `can` prefix | `isSubmitted`, `canReact` |
| Tests | mirror the file, `.test.ts` | `submit-drawing.test.ts` |
| Database | snake_case tables and columns, plural tables | `submission_channels` |
| Flag keys | dotted, area first | `canvas.full_toolset` |

Avoid abbreviations that are not universal. `submission`, not `sub`. The tenth
reader is not the author.

---

## 6. Enforcement

Every rule above is checked by a machine, in this order of preference: the type
system, then the linter, then a test, then CI, and only then a review comment.

**Dependency boundaries.** A committed `dependency-cruiser` configuration
encoding section 2 as rules, run in CI and failing the build on violation. This
is the single highest-value guardrail in the repo: it is the difference between
an architecture and a diagram of one.

**The specific forbidden edges to encode**, at minimum:

- `components/ui` -> `services`, `stores`, `data`, `features`
- `stores` -> `services`, `data`
- `services` -> `react`, `stores`, `features`
- `lib` -> anything except `contracts`
- `features/A` -> `features/B/**` except `features/B/index.ts`
- `app/**` -> `services`, `data`
- `backend/routes` -> `repositories`
- `backend/repositories` -> `services`, `routes`
- `backend/authz` -> the feature-flag client
- anything -> a banned directory name
- `lib/**`, `stores/**`, `data/**`, `features/**/actions/**`,
  `features/**/selectors/**` -> `react-native`'s `Platform`. Platform branching
  belongs in a `services/` adapter or in styling, per section 3b. This is the one
  rule that decides whether Android is a port or a rewrite

**Lint rules beyond the defaults:**

- `no-restricted-imports` for the zones above, as a second net
- no raw hex colours under `components/` or `app/`
- no `console.*` in `backend/src/` outside the logger
- no SQL template literals outside `repositories/`
- no `any`, no non-null assertion, no unchecked `as`
- import cycles are an error, not a warning

**Tests that assert structure**, because some rules are easier to test than to
lint:

- no module under `backend/src/authz/` imports the flag client
- the submit-to-unlock and channel-isolation bypass probes
- every declared flag has an owner, and every release flag has a `removeBy`

**CI gates:** typecheck, lint, dependency-cruiser, tests, secret scan,
dependency audit at an agreed threshold, and the web export. All of them block a
merge. See `ci-cd.md`.

---

## 7. When a rule is wrong

Some of this will be wrong. A boundary that seemed right in Sprint 0 will fight
a real feature in Sprint 2. When that happens:

**Do not quietly add an exception to the config.** Change the rule deliberately,
in an ADR, with the reason. A dependency-cruiser allowlist that grows one entry
per sprint is an architecture decaying in public, and it is worse than no rule
because it looks like one.

If the answer is genuinely "this code has nowhere to live," that is a finding
worth surfacing, not a gap to paper over. Add it to `code-questions.md`.
